Sam (Design): quick one — posted a screenshot of the playground when a tool call returns structured output: https://figma.com/file/xyz (preview) Sam (Design): problem: folks can't tell if that gray mini-card is the tool output or the assistant's final message. Rina (DevEx): yes — I've seen support tickets about "which step produced this". breadcrumbs could help: e.g., `Tool: excel_extract > table` above the payload. Marcus (Frontend): implementation note: stacking a breadcrumb + small tag is cheap, but streaming chunks may cause layout jump. prefer inline small label inside the card header. Hugo (A11y): flag: ensure any label is exposed to screen readers. if it's dynamic we need `aria-live="polite"` only for status changes, not for content. also keyboard focus must land on card when user tabs through results. Ava (PM): important: we need telemetry on whether users expand the tool card vs dismiss. add event `playground_tool_card_interaction`. Sam (Design): option A: breadcrumb + light divider above card (compact). option B: header pill in top-right with tool name + role (less vertical space). which do we prefer? :thinking_face: Marcus (Frontend): leaning B for stable layout. sample markup I mocked: ```html
excel_extract 
...json...
``` Marcus (Frontend): note CSS needs high-contrast token for pill and focus ring for button. Hugo (A11y): also add `role=\"group\" aria-label=\"Tool output: excel_extract\"` on the card wrapper. that gives screen readers context without relying on visual crumbs. Rina (DevEx): UX nit: label text should be short — tool id can be long (excel_extract_2026). show friendly name + hover full id. Ava (PM): agree on friendly name. +1 on telemetry. can we include a small "source" icon so users can quickly scan? (tool icon or badge) Sam (Design): I'll make two mocks (pill vs breadcrumb) and include hover state for full id + icon. planning to test with 3 power users tomorrow morning. CI-bot: Figma link updated by Sam (Design) — https://figma.com/file/xyz?node-id=45:2 :white_check_mark: Rina (DevEx): quick accessibility checklist before shipping: contrast, focus order, screenreader label, keyboard expand/collapse, and streaming behavior (no sudden aria-live floods). can someone own this? @Hugo? Hugo (A11y): I can take the a11y checklist. I'll pair with Marcus during implementation to review DOM semantics. Marcus (Frontend): I'll pick up the frontend work after mocks land. rough ETA: 2 dev days. Sam (Design): thanks all — small ask: react with :thumbsup: for option B (pill) or :busts_in_silhouette: for option A (breadcrumb) so we can quickly decide before the user tests. Ava (PM): :thumbsup: for B Marcus (Frontend): :thumbsup: Hugo (A11y): :thumbsup: Rina (DevEx): :busts_in_silhouette: (lean breadcrumb but ok with B if space wins) Sam (Design): notes captured. will iterate and drop final mocks and a short test script.
